title: INTEGRATE (germlINe tesTing rEGistry pRostATe cancEr) - Establishing inclusion criteria for germline testing and a family registry for patients with prostate cancer: A prerequisite for risk-adapted preventive measures
summary: The aim of the INTEGRATE study is to adapt and continuously improve the care of patients with prostate cancer as well as prevention and early detection for men who do not have the disease in line with their personal risk of developing the disease. As part of the study, information on the patient's medical history and any other cancers that may have occurred in the family is recorded. In addition, genetic tests are carried out to determine whether there are changes in genes that are associated with an increased risk of prostate cancer.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Histologically confirmed prostate cancer
- Treatment/clinical management at one of the participating centers in Germany
- Fulfillment of at least one indication criterion for constitutional genetic testing (according to the National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines)
- Written informed consent to participate in the study
- Written informed consent for genetic testing
- Sufficient language proficiency and willingness to adhere with study procedures
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of capacity to provide informed consent or refusal/withdrawal of consent to participate in the study, to data collection within the registry, or to genetic testing
- Insufficient availability of biological samples or refusal to permit the transfer of data/samples in pseudonymized form
- Sporadic prostate cancer, provided that the indication criteria for constitutional genetic testing are not met
